title: Claim Frequency Step Taken Off the Coverage Share
content:
# Counter Card: The Claim Frequency Step Taken Off the Coverage Share

Where a protection coverage answers for bench work at the Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service, a step is taken off the share that coverage carries according to how many claims stand filed against it in the twelve months to the handling date. The claims are counted from the Belrose Jewelry Protection and Care Plans records.

| Claims standing filed against the coverage in the twelve months to the handling date | How the coverage stands | Step taken off the share |
|---|---|---|
| More than one | in force | the frequent-claim step, 8 percent |
| Exactly one | in force | the single-claim step, 4 percent |
| Any other case | | no step is taken off the share on this ground |

**Clause.** Where more than one claim stands filed against the coverage in the twelve months to the handling date and the coverage stands in force, the frequent-claim step of 8 percent is taken off the share; where exactly one claim stands filed in that window and the coverage stands in force, the single-claim step of 4 percent is taken off. In any other case no step is taken off the share on this ground.

**Counting.** The window is the twelve months running back from the handling date, and what is counted is the claims standing filed against that coverage within it. A claim filed thirteen months ago falls outside the window. Where the coverage does not stand in force, neither step is taken off however many claims stand filed.

**Hypothetical readings.** A coverage in force with 3 claims filed in the last twelve months carries the frequent-claim step of 8 percent. The same coverage with 1 claim filed in that window carries the single-claim step of 4 percent. With no claim filed in the window, no step is taken off; and where the coverage stands out of good standing with 3 claims filed in the window, no step is taken off either.
